components.name: Parser Hebbian training (the FIXED, fact-count-INDEPENDENT cost)

components.verdict: DOMINATES the tiny-demo 112s (5 facts add little). Each is a fresh-bridge _initialize_simulation_data + a long single-threaded step loop. PAID EVERY LOAD; never persisted today.
components.important: At CHAT time the parser is exercised ONLY when the user TEACHES a new fact in the live console (hear() -> parser.parse). For a LOADED brain the saved facts are re-stored via comp.store() DIRECTLY (developed_brain_io._restore_facts), BYPASSING the parser. So a read-only chat session never needs the trained parser at all -- yet pays the full ~75K-step training.

components.name: Per-fact RF resonate re-store (the PER-FACT cost; grows with the brain's knowledge)

Called for EVERY fact: load (_restore_facts -> comp.store) and the self-knowledge re-teach loop (brain_chat_tui:376 inner.hear).

components.verdict: The result of store() is the numpy COMPOSITE phases array `comp` cached in composer.kb[i] = (fact, comp) (enable_substrate_store=False default). So the RF resonate output per fact IS just a [D] numpy array -- it is recomputed every load but is trivially serializable.

load_cost_breakdown.headline: TWO loops dominate: (1) ~75K-step parser training (FIXED, fact-independent -> dominates tiny-demo 112s) and (2) ~832-step-per-fact RF resonate (-> dominates the 52-fact SK brain). BOTH are pure recomputation of state that could be persisted; NEITHER is persisted today. load_developed_brain does NOT re-train any composer -- it re-RESONATES each fact via comp.store, and the agent constructor re-TRAINS the parser.

what_save_checkpoint_load_checkpoint_per.persists: cp_connections CSR (data/indices/indptr) [the parser's TRAINED Hebbian weights live here], membrane V, conductances, external current, firing states, traits, refractory, adex_w, ou, stp_u/x, last_spike_time, plastic mask.
what_save_checkpoint_load_checkpoint_per.does_NOT_persist: firing thresholds, STP recovery, eligibility traces (documented CLAUDE.md gotcha -> a loaded parser self-recovers in ~10ms of free-running, fine for inference); AND -- crucially for the composer -- the RF COMPLEX weights (cp_rf_w_re/im) are NOT in save_checkpoint's array list, and the composer's numpy kb composites are not bridge state at all.
what_save_checkpoint_load_checkpoint_per.implication: save_checkpoint is the RIGHT tool to persist the PARSER (its trained weights are in cp_connections). It is the WRONG tool for the composer fact-store (kb composites are numpy, not bridge arrays; and the per-op RF bridges are ephemeral). The composer store is better persisted as the kb composites themselves (already a numpy array per fact).

ranked_options_cheapest_first.name: Persist the composer fact-store composites (kb) in the bundle -> SKIP per-fact RF resonate on load
ranked_options_cheapest_first.mechanism: developed_brain_io already writes facts.json + grounded_codes.npz. ADD a kb_composites.npz: {fact_index -> comp[D] float32} extracted from composer.kb (the numpy composite each store() already computed). On load, instead of _restore_facts calling comp.store() (4 RF resonate windows/fact), set composer.kb = [(fact_dict, comp_array)] directly from the saved composites. Byte-identical to re-resonating (the composite IS the resonate output; deterministic per seed/codes). The fact dicts already round-trip via facts.json.
ranked_options_cheapest_first.reusable_vs_build: REUSE developed_brain_io.extract_facts + the npz machinery; BUILD a small extract_kb_composites()/load path (~30-40 lines, runner-only). NO sim/ edit.
ranked_options_cheapest_first.expected_speedup: Removes ~43K RF steps for the 52-fact SK brain (the part that makes SK 'longer'); ~4K for tiny-demo. Cuts the per-fact term to ~0. Dominant win for KNOWLEDGE-RICH brains (the artificial-life trajectory grows facts daily).
ranked_options_cheapest_first.caveat: Only addresses the per-fact term -- the ~75K-step parser training (option 2) still dominates tiny-demo. Best stacked with #2/#3.

ranked_options_cheapest_first.name: Make the agent parser LAZY (deferred) for a read-only LOADED brain -> SKIP ~75K-step parser training entirely
ranked_options_cheapest_first.mechanism: The parser is only used by hear() when the user TEACHES a new fact at runtime. A LOADED brain restores facts via comp.store() (no parser). So defer BridgeParser + AttributedBridgeParser construction+training until the FIRST runtime hear()/teach. Add a default-OFF constructor flag (e.g. defer_parser=True) on BrainConversationalAgent that sets self.parser/_attr_parser to a lazy builder; load_developed_brain passes it (a loaded brain is read-mostly). First teach in the console pays the ~75K steps ONCE; pure-Q&A sessions NEVER pay it.
ranked_options_cheapest_first.reusable_vs_build: REUSE the existing defer_train plumbing already in BridgeParser (defer_train param) + AttributedBridgeParser pattern. BUILD a lazy-property wrapper in BrainConversationalAgent + a load_developed_brain kwarg (~40-60 lines, runner-only). NO sim/ edit.
ranked_options_cheapest_first.expected_speedup: Removes the ENTIRE fixed ~75K-step cost for any session that doesn't teach a new fact -- i.e. the dominant term of the tiny-demo 112s and a large chunk of SK. The owner's 'talk to a developed brain' usage is overwhelmingly Q&A (read), so this is near-100% hit-rate.
ranked_options_cheapest_first.caveat: If a session DOES teach, the first teach is slow (one-time). Mitigate by also persisting trained parser weights (sub-option 2b) so even the first teach loads instead of trains:

sub_option_2b_persist_parser.mechanism: Persist each parser bridge via SimulationBridge.save_checkpoint (its trained cp_connections weights). On load, build the parser bridge skeleton + load_checkpoint + a short free-run to recover the unsaved thresholds (the documented ~10ms self-recovery), instead of _train(). BridgeParser/AttributedBridgeParser get a save_state(path)/load_state(path) pair writing under <bundle>/parser/.
sub_option_2b_persist_parser.reusable: REUSE bridge.save_checkpoint/load_checkpoint (cp_connections IS the trained weight). BUILD save_state/load_state on the two parser classes (~50 lines, runner-only). NO sim/ edit.
sub_option_2b_persist_parser.expected_speedup: Turns the first-teach parser cost from ~75K training steps into an HDF5 load + ~20-step recovery (<1s). Stacks with the lazy default so a Q&A session skips it and a teaching session loads-not-trains.

ranked_options_cheapest_first.name: Warm the brains at webapp STARTUP (cheap stopgap; hides latency, doesn't remove it)
ranked_options_cheapest_first.mechanism: Add an @app.on_event('startup') (the server ALREADY has two at server.py:1692/1701) that pre-builds + caches the default brains (tiny-demo, self-knowledge, the develop_gpu bundle) into _BRAIN_CHATS under a 'warm' session key in a background thread, so the owner's first real turn hits the warm cache. Optionally gate behind an env flag (BRAIN_CHAT_WARM=1) to keep dev startup fast.
ranked_options_cheapest_first.reusable_vs_build: REUSE _build_chat_brain + _BRAIN_CHATS + the existing startup-hook pattern. BUILD a ~20-line startup warmer (threaded so it doesn't block uvicorn boot). NO sim/ edit.
ranked_options_cheapest_first.expected_speedup: Owner first-turn latency -> ~warm (0.2-2.8s) for the pre-warmed brains. Does NOT reduce the actual build cost (still ~112s/9min, just moved to boot). Independent of #1/#2 -- complementary; best is #1+#2 (make the build itself fast) THEN optionally #3 to also hide the now-small residual.

ranked_options_cheapest_first.name: Cache the fully-built ChatBrain to disk (pickle) -- NOT recommended
ranked_options_cheapest_first.mechanism: Pickle the live ChatBrain/agent (incl. per-op RF bridges + parser bridges) after first build; unpickle on next load.
ranked_options_cheapest_first.reusable_vs_build: Would need custom __reduce__ for SimulationBridge (cupy arrays, h5 handles, CUDA-graph state) -- fragile, large, GPU-context-bound, version-brittle.
ranked_options_cheapest_first.expected_speedup: Unknown/risky; likely SLOWER than #1+#2 to deserialize cupy state and re-bind CUDA. REJECTED in favor of the structured persistence (#1 codes/composites + #2b parser checkpoint), which is the project's existing pattern (developed_brain_io bundle + bridge HDF5).

recommendation.single_best_cheapest_first_step: OPTION 2 (lazy parser for a loaded brain) -- it removes the dominant fact-INDEPENDENT ~75K-step parser training for the overwhelmingly-common read-only Q&A session, is the smallest change (reuses the existing BridgeParser defer_train plumbing), needs NO sim/ edit, and is byte-identical for any session that never teaches (the parser was never going to be used). It alone collapses tiny-demo's ~112s to seconds.
recommendation.recommended_stack_for_full_fix: 2 (lazy parser) + 1 (persist kb composites -> skip per-fact RF resonate). Together they remove BOTH dominant loops: #2 kills the fixed parser cost, #1 kills the per-fact cost -> a 52-fact brain LOADS in ~bundle-deserialize time (low seconds) instead of ~9 min. Add 2b (persist parser weights) so even a teaching session loads-not-trains, and optionally #3 (startup warm) as a zero-risk stopgap to also pre-pay the small residual before the owner's first turn.
recommendation.sim_flags: NONE. Every recommended option is reuse-by-import / runner + webapp only. (#2 reuses the existing BridgeParser(defer_train=...) param; #2b reuses bridge.save_checkpoint/load_checkpoint, no new sim/ surface; #1 extends developed_brain_io; #3 reuses the existing @app.on_event('startup') hook.)
anti_cheat_controls: Round-trip EQUALITY: a loaded brain (lazy parser + persisted composites) must answer the FULL who/what + yes-no + abstain matrix BYTE-IDENTICALLY to a freshly-built+retaught brain (the persisted composite IS the deterministic resonate output; assert per-fact comp arrays match a fresh _encode within atol 1e-9).
MOAT preserved: the no-confab abstention must hold (0 false-accepts) on the loaded brain -- only the saved facts are in kb; an untaught cue still abstains.

First-TEACH correctness (option 2): after a lazy-loaded brain teaches a NEW fact in the console, the parser must build+work and the new fact must recall correctly (and, with 2b, a loaded-parser teach must equal a trained-parser teach).

Existing CI guards (tests/test_brain_conversational_agent.py, tests/test_one_brain_composer_agent.py, the developed_brain_io round-trip) must pass verbatim with the new defaults OFF for the standalone build path (byte-identical) and ON for the load path.
